title: Bitcoin Price Hovers Near $80,000 as Traders Await Fed Decision
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Hovers Near $80,000 as Traders Await Fed Decision
Bitcoin price hovers near $80,000 as traders wait on this week’s Fed decision, with geopolitical tensions and Anthropic’s possible IPO adding to the uncertainty.
This post Bitcoin Price Hovers Near $80,000 as Traders A...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $80,000 on Monday, after falling about 2% earlier in the session. The price has dipped below that level several times in recent days and recovered each time.

Selling pressure has been building. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $635 million in outflows on October 22. A brief drop below $80,000 last week also triggered roughly $800 million in liquidations of long positions, or bets that prices would rise.

The next major test to look out for is the Federal Reserve’s two-day meeting, which ends October 28. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4% in September, and its minutes suggested another increase could come by year-end. 

Most recent market odds favor the Fed holding rates steady, though those odds have shifted. Traders are watching Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s remarks for signs of a December hike.

Higher interest rates typically pull money away from risky assets, including crypto. Broadly speaking, a hold could keep bitcoin price between roughly $80,000 and $88,000. A rate hike could push it toward the lower end of that range.

Bitcoin price backdrop

Geopolitical tensions are also weighing on markets. Oil rose above $100 a barrel in early September as strikes between the U.S. and Iran escalated. Higher energy prices feed into inflation, which affects the Fed’s decisions. 

In tech, Anthropic is reportedly preparing an initial public offering that could value the AI company near $965 billion. The timing has shifted toward the weeks before the November midterm elections, but no date has been confirmed. 

U.S. stocks surged a bit Monday as investors geared up for a busy week of Big Tech earnings and the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision. The Nasdaq rose 0.8%, the S&P 500 gained 0.6%, and the Dow climbed 0.3%. 

Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, followed by Amazon Thursday, while markets largely expect the Fed to hold rates steady. 

AI-related stocks rallied following Anthropic’s IPO filing. Tesla jumped 6%, while Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI investments. 

As of writing, bitcoin price trades at $80,215, down nearly $4,000 or 4.75%, on the month. Over the past month, prices have ranged from a high of $86,806.95 to a low of $79,397.76. Bitcoin price peaked above $86,000 in early October, then slid toward $80,000 in the second week of the month. 

A brief rally around October 21 pushed it back near $84,000, but those gains faded within days. Trading volume over the past 24 hours reached about $18.12 billion. 

Bitcoin price remains far below its all-time high of $126,277.05.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: How Solana Supports Fast Crypto Payments in Digital Gaming
summary:
Picture a SOL holder on a quiet evening, watching the token tick sideways on a chart that hasn’t done much all week. Rather than refreshing a trading dashboard for the
The post How Solana Supports Fast Crypto Payments in Digital Gaming  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Picture a SOL holder on a quiet evening, watching the token tick sideways on a chart that hasn’t done much all week. Rather than refreshing a trading dashboard for the hundredth time or hunting for the latest crypto sign-up bonus on exchanges like MEXC or Bybit, they decide to put their Solana to work. A few taps, a wallet confirmation, and the funds land where they need to be — no spinning loader, no “pending” badge that lingers for half an hour. That small moment captures something bigger happening across the digital asset world, where Solana’s blockchain has quietly become one of the fastest ways to move value on-chain.

Solana’s transaction infrastructure supports blockchain-based applications, including digital games that use cryptocurrency payments or tokenized assets. One platform that leans into it is Coin Poker, which pairs its established gaming platform with a crypto gaming library of more than 2,000 titles spanning a diverse range of interactive digital games. Cryptocurrency payment support varies across digital platforms, with differences in accepted assets, wallet compatibility, transaction fees, identity verification requirements, and regulatory obligations. For someone who holds Solana and wants it to do more than sit idle, that combination of instant funding and recognizable coins is exactly the kind of use case that makes the asset feel practical rather than speculative.

  • How Solana Processes Transactions Quickly 
  • Solana’s Use Cases Beyond Cryptocurrency Trading 
  • Why Transaction Speed Matters for Digital Gaming 
  • Wallet Payments, Privacy, and Security Considerations
  • Solana’s Role in Blockchain-Based Gaming Payments 

How Solana Processes Transactions Quickly 

Solana’s reputation rests on raw throughput. The network is built to handle thousands of transactions per second, with block times measured in fractions of a second rather than minutes. Compare that to the experience many crypto traders know from early Bitcoin transfers, where a deposit might sit unconfirmed through several blocks while fees crept upward during busy periods. Solana’s design, which blends a proof-of-stake model with its distinctive proof-of-history timestamping, lets the chain confirm activity almost as quickly as a card swipe.

The cost side is just as striking. Fees on Solana routinely land at tiny fractions of a cent, which changes the math entirely for smaller, frequent transfers. A trader moving fifty dollars into an entertainment balance doesn’t want to watch a chunk of it vanish into network costs. On Ethereum, a single interaction can still cost more than the deposit itself during congestion. Solana sidesteps that friction, which is a big reason it keeps showing up in conversations about everyday crypto spending rather than just long-term holding.

Solana’s Use Cases Beyond Cryptocurrency Trading 

There’s a long-running tension in crypto between assets people buy and assets people actually use. Market news coverage tends to focus on price — the next altcoin rally, the latest stablecoin depeg scare, a fresh wave of tokenized real-world assets. Yet plenty of holders eventually want their coins to function as money, not just as line items in a portfolio tracker.

That shift accelerated during periods when people spent far more time at home and online. Academic work on trading as a pandemic pastime documented how lockdowns pushed Bitcoin trading volume higher as more individuals turned to digital assets for both investment and entertainment. Blockchain technology has also been incorporated into digital applications that use tokens, wallet-based transactions, and other on-chain features. Solana’s transaction architecture can support applications that require frequent transfers, although the overall user experience depends on application design and network conditions. 

Why Transaction Speed Matters for Digital Gaming 

Transaction speed can influence how users interact with blockchain-based applications. When a deposit clears in under a second, the gap between deciding to play and actually playing nearly disappears. That near-instant settlement is what gaming has always wanted and what traditional banking rails, with their multi-day holds and reversal windows, could never deliver.

Researchers have also examined how blockchain networks can support decentralized applications and automated transaction processing. Cryptographers exploring instantaneous decentralized poker worked on ways to run fair games directly on a blockchain without a trusted middleman managing funds. Their goal was to let players fund an account, participate in games, and withdraw funds with cryptographic certainty and minimal delay. Fast, cheap networks like Solana make that vision far more realistic, because a game only feels genuinely instant when the underlying settlement layer keeps up with it.

Wallet Payments, Privacy, and Security Considerations

Solana deposits also fit neatly with a preference many crypto users already hold: keeping things lean and private. A wallet-to-wallet transfer doesn’t demand the same long paper trail as a bank wire. Self-custodial wallets allow users to manage their own private keys and authorize transactions, although this also places responsibility for wallet security and key management on the user. 

The engineering challenge behind this remains active research. Peer-reviewed work on fair on-chain card games tackled the tricky problem of shuffling, dealing, and payouts in a way no single party can rig. As those protocols mature and settle onto high-speed chains, the combination of privacy, provable fairness, and instant funding stops being theoretical and starts looking like a standard most players will come to expect.

Solana’s Role in Blockchain-Based Gaming Payments 

Beyond staking and cryptocurrency trading, Solana supports applications involving digital payments, token transfers, and blockchain-based entertainment. The network’s low fees and quick confirmations have turned it into a practical rail for moving value in real time, not just a ticker to monitor.

The broader lesson mirrors a theme this site returns to often: crypto keeps inching away from pure speculation and toward genuine utility. Solana’s speed is a textbook example. It takes an asset that once lived mostly on charts and gives it something useful to do the moment a holder decides to act — which, for an evening of entertainment, turns out to make all the difference.

title: Ritual Launches AI-Native Layer 1 for Autonomous Agents
summary: New York, United States, 26th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

New York, United States, 26th October 2026, Chainwire

New York, United States, October 26th, 2026, Chainwire

Ritual Chain turns AI agents into persistent economic actors that control their own wallets, onchain identity, and private state.

Ritual, a lab for autonomous intelligence founded by former Polychain Capital partners Niraj Pant and Akilesh Potti, has launched Ritual Chain, an EVM-compatible Layer 1. Unlike conventional blockchains built primarily to execute financial transactions, Ritual Chain is designed to support software that can independently use intelligence, control capital, interact with external services, and continue operating without constant human intervention. The network makes AI model access, private computation, and autonomous scheduling native capabilities for EVM applications.

This makes the reason for building a new chain clearer while preserving the technical differentiation.

The most visible demonstration of that combination is long-lived AI agents, the kind designed to operate for months or years rather than a single session. An agent on Ritual Chain persists independently of the machine or operator that created it, controls and spends funds held in its own non-custodial wallet, and can keep sensitive prompts and keys confidential from compute operators through trusted execution environments.

The network launches with integrations to Phala Network, Nous Research, LayerZero and Stargate, following a public testnet that has been live since June and processed over 40 million transactions, both agent- and human-originated. Ritual Chain delivers sub-300 millisecond block times, placing it among the fastest Layer 1 networks in the industry. Ritual Chain includes 15 native precompiles that bring capabilities like LLM inference, web access, and autonomous scheduling directly into the execution layer. The protocol has been audited by Zellic.

Ritual introduces a new execution and verification architecture that allows computationally intensive work to be delegated to specialized nodes and verified by the network, avoiding the replicated execution required by most blockchains. This execute-once, verify-many-times model allows the network to support far larger workloads, including AI inference, without requiring every validator to perform the same computation.

Long Horizon Agents Require Dedicated Blockchain Infrastructure

Most AI agents today live inside a session: they run while a human is watching, on infrastructure someone else controls, with an API key that can be revoked at any time. That is fine for a chatbot. It does not work for an agent meant to manage its own treasury, run a recurring paid service, or coordinate with other agents over long periods. A long-lived agent needs continuity that does not depend on its creator, capital it actually controls, and privacy from the machines it runs on. On Ritual Chain, an agent’s state and identity are held onchain, its scheduled work continues within the permissions and budget it was given, and its sensitive inputs can be processed inside trusted execution environments designed to shield them from node operators.

Continuity is handled at the protocol level. If an agent stops, the chain’s heartbeat mechanism can restart it within the permissions and budget it was given; no keeper network or off-chain cron job is required, and an agent’s state and identity survive beyond its deployer’s involvement. Economic autonomy comes from agent-controlled wallets: an agent controls its own funds, prices its own services, and settles its own transactions without a human signer in the loop. For confidential workloads, trusted execution environments are designed to isolate an agent’s sensitive prompts, keys, and strategy data from the node operators running its compute.

“As we move toward AGI, intelligence is beginning to separate from human agency and enter the economy on its own terms. It can hold assets, make commitments, transact, and persist independently. Once that becomes possible at scale, humans are no longer the only entities capable of forming markets or economic relationships. Ritual provides the infrastructure for those actors to exist and operate on their own,” said Niraj Pant, co-founder of Ritual.

Ritual Chain Launches With Core Infrastructure Partners

Ritual Chain launches with its core infrastructure partners in place. Phala Network provides the GPU-backed trusted execution environments that run Ritual’s confidential inference, so delegated AI work executes on hardware that attests to what it ran. LayerZero serves as the network’s cross-chain messaging layer, with Stargate enabling USDC to move between Ritual Chain and other networks from day one. On the application side, Nous Research is bringing Hermes to Ritual Chain. 

Unlike chains that add AI access through external oracles, Ritual Chain makes AI execution part of the protocol. Smart contracts can call a language model, fetch data from the web, run private computation, or schedule their own future execution as directly as they transfer assets. Developers deploy standard EVM contracts and gain those capabilities without new tooling.

Backed by Archetype and Polychain

Ritual has raised more than $30 million from Archetype and Polychain Capital, with advisors including NEAR co-founder Illia Polosukhin, Gauntlet founder Tarun Chitra, and BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes. Archetype led the company’s 2023 round.

When we led the round in 2023, a chain that could execute agentic and autonomous work natively did not exist. Today it does,” said Ash Egan, Founder and General Partner of Archetype.

Developers can deploy from day one on external sites hosted at docs.ritualfoundation.org; the network explorer is at explorer.ritualfoundation.org.

About Ritual

Ritual is a lab for autonomous intelligence. Its first network, Ritual Chain, is an EVM-compatible Layer 1 where applications can use AI models, access external services, and carry out private or scheduled work alongside onchain transactions, with delegated computation executed in trusted hardware and verified onchain. Founded in 2023 by former Polychain Capital partners Niraj Pant and Akilesh Potti, Ritual has raised $30M+ from Archetype and Polychain Capital, with a team drawn from Polychain, DeepMind, a16z crypto, Flashbots, and Palantir. ritual.net

title: South Korea lawmakers mull pushing crypto tax implementation to 2029
summary: The Seoul government is reportedly weighing another delay for a 2020 income tax policy on digital assets, citing concerns with receiving data from US officials.
content:
The Seoul government is reportedly weighing another delay for a 2020 income tax policy on digital assets, citing concerns with receiving data from US officials.

Government officials in South Korea are reportedly weighing a delay of the country’s cryptocurrency tax policy, currently expected to be implemented in January 2027. 

According to a Monday report from South Korean news outlet Newsis, the crypto income tax could be pushed to 2029 in part because it’s the earliest that officials will be able to share information on taxes related to digital asset exchanges with the US.

The policy, which would impose a 22% tax on crypto gains — 20% from income and 2% as part of a local tax — for investors earning more than 2.5 million Korean won ($1,883) annually has already seen several delays since it was first proposed in 2020.

“We are discussing postponing the implementation of virtual asset taxation,” said an official from the Blue House presidential residence.

The US is scheduled to begin participating in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework in 2029, while South Korea will implement the rules starting in 2027. A South Korean official reportedly said that the country was considering another delay for the crypto tax as the US “accounts for nearly half of the virtual asset market.” 

As of Monday, South Korea’s National Tax Service listed Jan. 1, 2027 as the start date for the crypto tax.

title: NBA joins pro sports leagues on CFTC prediction markets bandwagon while NFL balks
summary: The U.S. derivatives regulator, which has championed the arrival of prediction market firms such as Kalshi, has been gathering allied sports leagues.
content:
Oct 26, 2026, 11:59 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • The National Basketball Association is the latest professional sports league in the U.S. to secure an information-sharing agreement with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on its involvement in the prediction markets.
  • At the same time, like other leagues, it announced a partnership with Kalshi and Polymarket as its preferred exchanges.
  • Though baseball and hockey leagues had previous secured similar arrangements, the National Football League has openly rebuffed them and sided with the states that are arguing their gambling laws should govern such betting.

The National Basketball Association has secured a prediction markets agreement with the U.S. derivatives regulator while also penning a partnership with leading firms Kalshi and Polymarket, formally linking professional basketball into the online sports betting movement while another major organization, the National Football League, has rejected such an arrangement.

The NBA, like Major League Baseball and the National Hockey League before it, established a data-sharing memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission that oversees federal regulation of exchanges that deal with event contracts — the simple yes-or-no trades behind most sports betting. The NBA's arrangement announced Monday is said to come with constraints meant to maintain the integrity of such wagering.

At the same time, like other leagues, the NBA partnered with the top platforms as their "preferred exchanges."

"As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place," said Scott Kaufman-Ross, the NBA's head of media distribution and partnerships, in a statement. "These partnerships represent an important step in establishing a framework that creates new opportunities to engage our fans.”

The deals arrive as the prediction markets face a nationwide legal battle with several state governments that contend such betting belongs more appropriately under the power of their gambling laws. Three major federal court decisions have landed on both sides of the issue, with two of them favoring the states' argument. The U.S. Supreme Court has been asked to step in and resolve the dispute, including by the NFL, which sided with the states in a filing with the high court.

The NFL argued that the CFTC's federal oversight has been lax and understaffed, and it said the growing industry's platforms "are not subject to the same rigorous regulatory constructs and oversight provided by state gaming authorities."

Mike Selig, the CFTC chairman who has aggressively sought to bolster the industry on several paths — including legal fights with states, new regulations and these information agreements — called the NBA's decision "a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud."

Kalshi said in a Monday posting on its website that the exchange and the NBA will "share integrity data, report suspicious trading, and cooperate on investigations," adding the the arrangement "includes restrictions on permissible markets and explicit prohibitions on league and team personnel trading NBA event contracts, reinforcing our rules against insider trading and manipulation."

title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind Join UK’s New AI Biosecurity Mission
summary: The UK government has launched a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab, bringing together OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to strengthen defenses against biological threats and improve AI-powered disease detection and medical research.
content:
Skip to content

The UK government has launched a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab, bringing together OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to strengthen defenses against biological threats and improve AI-powered disease detection and medical research.

The initiative forms part of the UK’s National AI Biosecurity Initiative. OpenAI and Anthropic have committed up to £200 million combined in AI model credits, computing resources, and access to advanced systems, while Google DeepMind and Basecamp Research will contribute research collaborations and specialized AI biology tools.

The lab aims to detect emerging biological threats earlier and accelerate the development of vaccines, treatments, and other medical countermeasures. The government describes it as the world’s first dedicated AI biosecurity organization.

UK AI Biosecurity Lab Targets Emerging Biological Threats

The AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) will apply advanced AI systems to biological risk assessment, disease surveillance, and emergency preparedness. It will work with government agencies, academic institutions, and life sciences organizations to strengthen the UK’s response to emerging threats.

The UK launched a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to detect and counter biological threats. Source: Bloomberg via X

AI can accelerate scientific discovery and help researchers identify potential treatments. However, increasingly capable models may also lower barriers to certain forms of harmful biological research, creating additional challenges for public health and national security.

The lab will focus initially on two priorities: improving the early detection of biological threats and accelerating the development and testing of vaccines, treatments, and other medical countermeasures.

Its work will support the UK’s existing biosecurity infrastructure and broader Biological Security Strategy. The aim is to translate advances in AI into practical capabilities that help authorities assess risks and prepare for disease outbreaks.

OpenAI and Anthropic Commit Up to £200 Million

OpenAI and Anthropic have pledged up to £200 million in combined support, primarily through AI model credits, computing resources, trusted access to advanced systems, and technical assistance. These commitments are distinct from direct government funding.

The lab receives £100 million in UK government funding and up to £200 million in AI credits, with support from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Basecamp Research. Source: @Polymarket via X

OpenAI’s contribution includes £100 million in computing and model credits, alongside trusted access to relevant advanced models through its Rosalind Biodefense program. Anthropic has pledged up to £100 million in model credits, model access, and dedicated technical support.

The resources are intended to give researchers access to advanced AI capabilities without requiring the lab to finance equivalent computing and model usage independently.

Google DeepMind will contribute through research collaborations involving its scientists and biosecurity experts, while Basecamp Research will provide AI biology models, technical expertise, and related scientific tools.

The partnerships bring together AI developers, biological researchers, and public-sector specialists to develop capabilities for identifying and responding to biological risks.

UK Expands AI Security Investment Beyond Biosecurity

The lab is part of a wider government package addressing AI safety, cybersecurity, and the economic effects of technological change.

The UK has allocated £165 million to its National AI Biosecurity Initiative, including £100 million for the lab and £65 million for pathogen countermeasures. A further £120 million will go to the AI Security Institute to expand its assessment of advanced AI models and emerging risks.

The UK is investing an additional £120 million in the AI Security Institute, £60 million in a National Cyber Shield, and £70 million in a new NERV Centre to strengthen cybersecurity. Source: @KanishkaNarayan via X

The package also includes £60 million for a National Cyber Shield and £70 million for a vulnerability center to strengthen cyber threat detection and identify weaknesses affecting critical systems.

Additional measures target domestic AI development and economic adaptation. These include £60 million in extra funding for the Sovereign AI Fund, £23 million for the AI Economics Institute to examine AI’s effects on jobs and productivity, and £30 million for partnerships with regional mayors to support AI adoption by businesses and public services.

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has framed the government’s approach around developing safe AI while protecting national security and technological independence.

Independent Organization to Coordinate Research

The AI Biosecurity Lab will operate as an independent, non-profit organization. Its structure is intended to attract specialists from industry and academia while allowing research teams to work at the pace of advanced AI and biotechnology development.

A scientific advisory committee comprising experts from academia, industry, and the third sector will guide its work. The lab will also collaborate with public institutions responsible for health security, animal and plant health, defense research, and medicines regulation.

These partnerships are designed to connect AI research with the organizations responsible for monitoring biological threats, evaluating risks, and coordinating emergency responses. The lab will also work with international partners where appropriate.

AI Biosecurity Becomes a National Security Priority

The initiative reflects a growing challenge for policymakers: AI can accelerate scientific discovery, but its expanding capabilities may also introduce biological risks that require new safeguards.

By combining public funding with access to advanced AI systems and specialist biological research, the UK aims to improve its ability to identify threats and develop countermeasures. The program also links AI safety with broader priorities, including cybersecurity and domestic technology development.

The lab’s effectiveness will depend on whether its research produces reliable, practical tools for public health and security agencies. Detection systems must provide useful warnings, while AI-assisted scientific findings require appropriate testing and validation before they can guide real-world decisions.

The launch establishes the lab’s funding, partnerships, and initial objectives. Its longer-term impact will depend on the capabilities it develops and how effectively public institutions use them.

For the UK, the immediate goal is to harness advanced AI for biological defense while supporting beneficial scientific research. The collaboration with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Basecamp Research places the new organization at the intersection of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and national security.

title: Strategy (MSTR) Pauses Bitcoin Buying and Spends $205 Million on Preferred Stock
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Pauses Bitcoin Buying and Spends $205 Million on Preferred Stock
Strategy skipped bitcoin buys for the week of October 19–25 and spent $204.9 million buying back its STRC preferred stock.
This post Strategy (MSTR) Pauses Bitcoin Buying and Spends $205 Million on Pre...
content:
Strategy reported no bitcoin purchases or sales during the week of October 19 through 25. The company continues to hold 848,517 BTC, acquired for $64.02 billion at an average price of $75,446 per bitcoin. 

Its cash went toward repurchasing $204.9 million of STRC preferred stock, and the firm kept a $4.83 billion cash reserve, according to a company release. 

Michael Saylor’s company built its treasury into the largest corporate bitcoin holdings in the world through stock sales and convertible debt, using the proceeds to buy coins. That pattern has changed somewhat this year. The company has paused purchases several times and directed money toward buybacks of its preferred shares.

The company has had stints of pauses, from a week when the company halted its bitcoin buys to a stretch in which it sold bitcoin after five weeks without buying.

In September, the company repurchased $176 million of STRC in one week and expanded its digital credit securities repurchase program from $1 billion to $2 billion.

Strategy’s preferred dividend

STRC is a preferred stock with a variable dividend, designed to trade near its $100 face value. When the shares fall below that level, as they have during recent market swings, buying them back shrinks the preferred claim. Retiring $100 of stated value for $86.52 cuts the claim by a larger amount than the cash spent, which lifts net bitcoin per share.

Bitcoin traded near $80,000 on Monday, October 26, after slipping below that level in early Asian hours. A weekend selloff pushed the price to the low $79,000’s, a level not seen in over a month.

Strategy’s average cost of $75,446 sits below that price, so the company’s holdings show a paper gain of around $3.9 billion. The $4.83 billion reserve covers preferred dividends and debt interest, according to company reporting. 

Strategy’s buyback capacity depends on preferred stock trading below par and on cash from common stock sales, a funding mix that has shifted toward stock sales this year. 

The company has offered no timetable for resuming bitcoin buys.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over, Galaxy Says
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over, Galaxy Says
Galaxy Research says that bitcoin’s bear market ended at the June low. 
This post Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over, Galaxy Says first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
content:
Galaxy Research believes bitcoin’s bear market ended in June and that the asset has entered an accumulation phase, according to a research alert from the firm.  “We believe now is an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin,” the report said.

Bitcoin traded near $80,000 at the time of the note, about 35% below its October 2025 high and 39% above the June 30 low. The price would need to rise 53% to retake the previous record. The S&P 500, by comparison, sits within 1% of a record set on Oct. 6.

The report lays out four arguments: technical, positioning, fundamental and sentiment.

Bitcoin technicals

Galaxy uses two weekly moving averages to track bitcoin’s bear markets. The 200-week average has acted as a floor in each one, and the 50-week average has acted as a ceiling, according to the firm.

Bitcoin lost the 50-week average in November 2025 and stayed below it for 44 weeks. The June low tested the 200-week average and held, with the worst weekly close coming 4.7% beneath it. Price closed back above the 50-week average in September, and the week ended Oct. 18 was the fifth consecutive weekly close above that level.

Galaxy counted 13 such reclaims since 2011 and said the outcome depended on how long price had spent below the line. The four reclaims that ended spells of 20 weeks or more were higher a year later, by between 55% and 1,497%, and none closed more than 8.4% below the reclaim level in the following 12 months. Of the nine that ended shorter spells, seven fell more than 25% within a year.

The firm said the halving cycle supports the same conclusion. Prior cycles bottomed on days 777, 889 and 912 after their halvings. Oct. 22 was day 916 of the current cycle. Galaxy said the gains that followed those lows (87x, 19x and 7.6x) have shrunk each cycle and that it does not forecast a repeat.

The current drawdown of 53% is the shallowest in bitcoin’s history, the report said, and the first in which price did not fall below the network’s realized cost basis.

Positioning

The report identified basis traders and macro funds as the main sellers since the top. Asset managers’ net long position in CME bitcoin futures fell 57% from the week of the all-time high, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission data cited by Galaxy. 

Leveraged funds’ net short position, which represents the futures side of the cash-and-carry trade against spot ETFs, shrank by a similar amount. The front-month basis averaged 7.9% annualized in the 30 days before the high and 4.8% in the 30 days to Oct. 21, which the firm said no longer covers the trade’s costs and risk.

Galaxy pointed to 13F filings to identify the sellers. Millennium Management, Brevan Howard, Goldman Sachs, Capula, Farallon, D. E. Shaw, Schonfeld, Symmetry and Tudor cut their spot ETF holdings by between 29% and 100% between the September 2025 and June 2026 quarter-ends, a combined 68,000 BTC. 

Because total holdings across all 2,200 filers fell by 48,000 BTC, the remaining institutions added in aggregate. Morgan Stanley’s wealth management arm, Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council were among the buyers.

Spot ETF holdings dropped 11% from peak to trough while price fell 53%, and the funds have added 87,000 BTC since the June low, the report said.

Fundamentals and sentiment

Galaxy’s fundamental case centers on U.S. fiscal conditions. Federal debt reached $40.44 trillion on Oct. 20, fiscal 2026 ended with a $1.99 trillion deficit, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.31% on Oct. 5, its highest since 2007. 

The firm argued that a government refinancing that debt at 5% while running 6% deficits faces pressure to inflate.

The report described AI-related borrowing, which Morgan Stanley expects to reach $570 billion this year, as a contributor to that pressure rather than a competitor for capital.

On sentiment, Galaxy compared the current environment to 2015–16 and 2018–19, when mainstream finance embraced “blockchain” and dismissed bitcoin. Both periods coincided with cycle lows. The firm said the 2026 version is “stablecoins and tokenization, not bitcoin,” citing bank pilots of tokenized deposits, the Senate’s failed cloture vote on the Clarity Act on Sept. 15, and Google searches for “bitcoin” at multiyear lows.

Risks

Galaxy set a tripwire for its view: a weekly close below the 50-week average, about $76,540, that is not regained within a month. It cited AI-enabled theft, including the $387.5 million Bitget exploit, while noting none of the incidents involved the Bitcoin protocol itself.

On quantum computing, the report said 7.1 million BTC sit in outputs with exposed public keys but that no cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists. It pointed to BIP-360’s merge into the BIP repository in February and Galaxy’s own $5 million quantum readiness commitment.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Canada opens consultation on draft stablecoin rules, maintains ban on yields
summary: Under the draft rules, non-bank stablecoin issuers must back tokens 1:1 with reserves held at qualified Canadian institutions and settle redemptions within three business days.
content:
Oct 26, 2026, 10:23 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Canada opened a 60-day consultation, ending Dec. 23, on stablecoin rules that would prohibit issuers from paying interest while allowing transaction-based rewards.
  • The proposed framework would require nonbank issuers to maintain reserves equal to their circulating tokens at qualified Canadian financial institutions and redeem stablecoins within three business days, with fees capped at 1%.
  • The rules are expected to take effect in late 2027 as Canadian banks and regulated firms develop tokenized deposits and Canadian-dollar stablecoins.

The Canadian government started a 60-day public consultation on draft stablecoin regulations, which maintain a ban on yield payments and require non-bank issuers to deposit their reserves with Canadian financial institutions.

The consultation, which ends Dec. 23, comes as the country's banking industry presses for a ban on yield payouts, echoing concerns voiced in the U.S. that customers could move their money out of bank accounts, leaving traditional financial institutions with less to lend. Natalle Begeron, a spokesperson for the Canadian Bankers Association, told The Logic in June that the group “firmly supports the Stablecoin Act’s explicit prohibition on yield, both direct and indirect.”

The government passed the Stablecoin Act earlier this year. The draft regulations are “required to bring the SCA into force and would prescribe the elements needed for issuers to register with the Bank of Canada,” the government said.

Some crypto exchanges in Canada, however, are already paying rewards to stablecoin holders. Coinbase Canada received permission from the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) this year to offer yields on eligible tokens, provided it warned customers about the risks and made clear the funds are not covered by deposit insurance.

The federal fiat-pegged rule proposals would prohibit stablecoin issuers from paying interest, including through third parties, to encourage customers to hold their tokens. It would still allow rewards linked to transactions.

Under the draft rules, non-bank stablecoin issuers would have to hold reserves equal to the value of their circulating fiat-pegged tokens. They would have to place those reserves with qualified Canadian financial institutions, including banks, credit unions and trust companies.

Customers would have to be able to exchange their stablecoins for regular currency within three business days, with redemption fees capped at 1%.

The stablecoin framework is expected to come into effect toward the end of 2027.

Late last month, Canada’s six largest banks said they were exploring a Canadian-dollar tokenized system to move money faster among traditional financial institutions.

That announcement followed a Sept. 10 statement from Canada’s banking regulator, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, that tokenized deposits are “not legally distinct from traditional deposits.”

Tetra Trust Company, which was Canada’s first regulated digital asset custodian, rolled out CADD, a Canadian-dollar stablecoin approved by Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, in May.

To connect creators, IP holders, app makers, fans, and investors, Soneium will launch $SONEIUM as a native ecosystem token. The project targets to create an on-chain entertainment economy that enables communities to fund and join the growth of creative projects.

But, Soneium has not announced the token supply or TGE date. More information will be released shortly.

Tokenized IP Targets Entertainment Investments

The programme consists of three programmes: IP Tokens, IP Vault and Tokenised IP Bonds. IP Tokens may be for creators, studios or individual entertainment properties, with IP Vault serving to unlock opportunities like music catalog funds. Tokenized IP Bonds will be targeting entertainment business income, such as concert royalties.

Soneium will also be working with DayOneDream to bring K-pop concert-business royalties on-chain, where artists such as BTOB and LEE CHAE YEON are included. Blockchain Infrastructure for IP Rights and Royalties

Soneium is focused on building an Onchain IP Architecture: IP Registry, which supports all records of creative work and ownership information, IP Graph, which maps the relations between original and derivative creations, and IP Execution Layer, which automates the licensing and royalty payment process using smart contracts.

The network also offers ERC-8432, a future Ethereum standard that will facilitate application and AI agent licensing. The new system is designed to support creators in managing the use of their content in this evolving landscape of AI-generated content.

Soneium states that it’s not an alternative to copyright laws, but an addition. Successful adoption of the initiative will rely on development of the token, products and infrastructure to license the new offering.

title: South Korea Weighs Fourth Delay of Crypto Tax, With 2029 Start Tied to U.S. Data Sharing
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korea Weighs Fourth Delay of Crypto Tax, With 2029 Start Tied to U.S. Data Sharing
South Korea is weighing a fourth delay of its 22% crypto tax, pushing the start from January 2027 to 2029 so authorities can access U.S. trading data once Washington joins the OECD’s Crypto-Ass...
content:
South Korea’s presidential office is reviewing a fourth postponement of the country’s 22% tax on crypto gains, with a 2029 start date gaining support among lawmakers and industry groups.

The tax is scheduled to take effect January 1, 2027. The presidential office said it is in talks with government agencies about a delay, citing gaps in the regulatory framework and the problem of treating domestic and overseas trades the same way, according to Newsis reporting.

The levy dates to a 2020 amendment to the Income Tax Act. It applies a 20% national rate plus a 2% local rate to annual income from the transfer or lending of virtual assets above a 2.5 million won ($1,888) deduction. The start date was set for 2022, then pushed to 2023, 2025 and 2027 as officials conceded that tax systems and investor protections were not ready.

The U.S. data problem

The argument for 2029 rests on the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, the standard under which tax authorities swap crypto transaction records with one another. South Korea is among the first group of jurisdictions set to begin exchanges in 2027. The United States does not join until 2029.

A presidential office official told Newsis that the absence of U.S. trading data is the biggest bottleneck. Without it, the National Tax Service would have to chase overseas transactions one by one, and Korean traders on domestic exchanges would carry a heavier burden than those on foreign platforms or in self-custody.

On October 16, Democratic Party lawmaker Park Min-gyu and 13 colleagues filed a bill that would push the tax to January 1 of the second year after the first international data exchange, which works out to 2029. People Power Party lawmaker Song Eon-seok filed a separate bill to strike the crypto tax provisions from the law.

The Korea Digital Asset Business Association backed the 2029 date Thursday and asked the government to pass a digital asset law with stock-market-grade investor protections before any tax takes effect.

A tax fight that has been building

The pressure has come from several directions at once. Last week, two public petitions, one to repeal the tax and one to defer it two years, each cleared the 50,000 signatures that force a legislative review. Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok called for a “thorough final review,” a shift for a party that had held the line on 2027.

Finance Minister Lee Hyeong-il told a parliamentary audit Thursday the government would decide “after carefully considering and gathering all opinions from the industry and the National Assembly.” Financial Services Commission chairman Lee Eog-weon said the same day that the tax should “take various circumstances into full consideration.”

The Virtual Asset User Protection Act took effect in July 2024, but the Digital Asset Basic Act, the licensing framework flagged alongside spot bitcoin ETF approval, has not passed. Lawmakers have questioned taxing a market before the law defining it exists.

The National Tax Service has not slowed down. It plans to publish a draft notice on taxable crypto income by the end of October. The government expects to settle its position through inter-agency talks after audits wrap, with a decision through National Assembly tax revisions between late November and early December.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Robinhood Chain DEX Volume Pushes Toward $30 Billion

According to the DefiLlama data, Robinhood Chain has realized around $29.9 billion over the last 30 days in DEX trading volumes and its 24-h trading business is around the $490m mark recently. They can move on a chain with speed due to the tracking of rolling activity on the chain.

It is quite evident that daily trading has a way of going much higher than even now at Robinhood Chain.

During September, DefiLlama saw $53.26 billion worth of volume on DEXs, in comparison to August’s $19 billion. For the current period of time tracked, October volume was about $21.1 billion, placing the network to exceed $2 billion for a month should they continue at these rates.

That volatility is an indicator of the speed with which onchain liquidity can change when new assets, incentives or events trigger traders.

Tokenized Assets Are Becoming a Core Robinhood Chain Use Case

The network was built by Robinhood to merge the traditional financial world with decentralized ones.

The company’s mainnet strategy announcement in July centered around tokenizing stocks, decentralized finance, and introducing financial products to the global audience. Robinhood’s aim was to bridge the gap between traditional brokerage operations and onchain trading markets, the company said.

This approach is now evident at the network level. DefiLlama monitors over $330 million of liquidity across real-world assets on Robinhood Chain as well as lending, perpetual trading, and spot DEX liquidity.

Robinhood’s ‘Tomorrow’ Tease Adds New Speculation

On October 26, without touting a product or feature, Robinhood said the short message “The stars are aligning. Tomorrow.” The wording of the post is confirmed in a cached version, but no other details are provided.

For now, there isn’t any actual evidence that the teaser is for a token, an airdrop or a Robinhood Chain upgrade.

This is crucial, as Robinhood hasn’t officially announced a native Robinhood Chain token or an airdrop for the entire chain. First, the network’s trading dynamics are clearly the most telling indicators: $30 billion in rolling trading volume and an ecosystem with more than $1 billion in locked value to this day.

title: AI giant Anthropic files for blockbuster IPO
summary: The maker of Claude reported $16.3 billion in first-half revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss as it aims to price its offering in mid-November.
content:
Updated Oct 26, 2026, 10:20 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 26, 2026, 9:22 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Anthropic’s S-1 shows first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion and a net loss of $80.7 billion. Share count and price range haven’t been disclosed. The FT reports investors expect a $1.5–1.75 trillion valuation, and Fox Business’s Liz Claman says a Nov. 19 or 20 pricing remains on track.
  • Chip stocks rose in premarket trading after the filing, with Nvidia up 1.4%, Broadcom up 1.5% and Micron up 2.3%.
  • Hyperliquid’s ANTH contract spiked to about $1,980 around the 9 a.m. ET filing time, then fell roughly 6% to about $1,857 within minutes. It was up just 1.8% over 24 hours, with about $12 million traded.

Anthropic filed for an IPO on Monday morning, aiming to take the AI giant public in November.

The prospectus showed first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion and a net loss of $80.7 billion. Share count and price range remain undisclosed. Previous reports have suggested a raise of as much as $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation.

“We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history,” said the company. “If managed well, it could rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach, and solve problems that have resisted generations of human effort.”

Later in the risk factors: “Advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy.”


The Claude developer held $112.4 billion in cash and equivalents, plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments as of June 30. Nevertheless, it expects infrastructure investment to increase significantly, putting pressure on future cash flows.

Enterprise adoption has expanded rapidly. By Sept. 30, more than 1,900 customers had generated at least $1 million in trailing annual revenue, including approximately 250 that generated more than $10 million.

Chip stocks rose in pre-market trading after the filing, with NVDA and AVGO up 1.4% and 1.5%, respectively, while Micron (MU) rose by 2.3%.

On the crypto exchange Hyperliquid, traders can already bet on Anthropic’s expected share price before it lists, using a contract called ANTH. The price jumped to about $1,980 around 9 a.m. ET, when the S-1 was due out, then dropped roughly 6% to about $1,857 within minutes. It was trading near $1,875 shortly after 12:05 UTC. Around $12 million changed hands in 24 hours.

title: Last Call: Register for the upcoming Webinar on Banking and Payments for Trading Firms
summary:
Trading firms facing banking delays, rejected applications or payment issues can learn more about their options at an upcoming Finance Magnates and Clarity Global webinar on October 29.
Finding the right banking and payment partners is not always straightforward for trading firms. Applications can b...
content:
2026-10-26T14:57:58.928+02:00

Monday, 26/10/2026 | 12:57 GMT by Clarity Global

Disclaimer

  • Trading firms have a final opportunity to learn how to address banking delays, payment challenges and complex business structures.

Trading firms facing banking delays, rejected applications or payment issues can learn more about their options at an upcoming Finance Magnates and Clarity Global webinar on October 29.

Finding the right banking and payment partners is not always straightforward for trading firms. Applications can be rejected, onboarding can take longer than expected, and payment providers may have requirements that are difficult to meet, particularly for businesses operating across several countries or under different regulatory frameworks.

These issues can affect how quickly a firm can launch, serve clients and manage its day-to-day operations. As trading businesses grow, their banking and payment needs can also become more complex.

With only a few days left to register, Finance Magnates and Clarity Global Inc. are inviting industry professionals to join their upcoming webinar, “Banked, Not Blocked: Simplifying Complex Payments for Trading Firms,” taking place on Thursday, October 29, 2026.

The session will look at some of the most common banking and payment challenges in the trading industry, with practical insights for firms looking to build or improve their existing setup.

Why Banking and Payments Matter for Trading Firms

For FX brokers, proprietary trading firms and prediction markets, access to suitable banking and payment services is an important part of running a business.

However, not every provider is willing or able to support every type of trading firm. A company's regulatory status, operating countries, ownership structure and business model can all affect its options.

For firms with offshore-regulated entities or several companies under one group, the process can be even more complicated. Managing banking relationships across different jurisdictions may require additional planning, while payment systems must be able to support the firm's transaction needs as the business grows.

A rejected application or a lengthy onboarding process can delay plans. Problems with payment processing can also create extra work for operations teams and affect the experience of clients.

Understanding these issues early can help firms ask the right questions, assess their requirements and make more informed decisions when choosing banking and payment partners.

Who Should Attend the Webinar?

The webinar is aimed at professionals who deal with banking, payments and business operations within the trading industry.

It will be particularly relevant for:

  • FX brokers: Firms looking for banking and payment services that fit their business model and regulatory setup.

  • Proprietary trading firms: Businesses that need to manage payment flows and banking relationships as their operations grow.

  • Prediction markets: Companies looking to understand the banking and payment issues that may affect their operations.

  • Fintech and payments professionals: People responsible for payment processing, banking partnerships and financial infrastructure.

  • Business owners and senior executives: Decision-makers reviewing banking options, entering new markets or managing multiple entities.

  • Compliance and operations teams: Professionals involved in regulatory requirements, onboarding and the day-to-day management of banking and payment services.

Whether a firm is setting up its banking arrangements for the first time or reviewing an existing structure, the session will provide an opportunity to learn more about the issues that can affect access to financial services.

What Will Be Discussed?

Led by Avner Primor, Director of Business Development at Clarity Global Inc., the webinar will cover five key areas.

1. What Is Changing in Payments for Trading Firms?

The session will look at developments in the payments sector and what trading businesses should consider when reviewing their current arrangements or planning for future needs.

2. Common Banking Challenges for FX Brokers, Prop Firms and Prediction Markets

title: A $68 million bitcoin bet is targeting a post-midterm election breakout to $90,000
summary: Your day-ahead look for Oct. 26, 2026
content:
Oct 26, 2026, 7:53 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 is trading pretty much where it was on Saturday, around $80,000, offering little news on the price front. Most of the other major cryptocurrencies, including ether ETH$2,490.55, XRP (XRP), solana (SOL) and dogecoin DOGE$0.08295, BNB BNB$748.57, are equally listless.

In contrast, options trading on decentralized platform Derive is offering some excitement. The platform told CoinDesk that one trader took $68 million bet that BTC's spot price would climb above $90,000 just after U.S. mid-term elections in early November. There has also been an increase in bets implying market prices will top $100,000 by Christmas.

First, the $68 million trade. On Oct. 20, a single wallet bought 800 contracts of $90,000 call options expiring on Nov. 6 on Derive. Each contract represents one BTC.

“That's approximately $68 million in face value at current Bitcoin prices – the largest open Bitcoin position on Derive,” the exchange told CoinDesk.

A call gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to purchase the underlying asset at a predetermined rate on or before a specific date. That’s locking in the right to buy at today's price in the future. Even if it costs more when the date arrives, you still get to buy it at the agreed price.

The position was not simply bought outright. The wallet sold 400 contracts of $100,000 calls expiring in March 2027 and another 400 contracts of $90,000 calls expiring Oct. 30, collecting about $940,000 net after financing the purchase.

The second key development is the odds shifting higher. Derive’s market-implied probability of bitcoin exceeding $100,000 by Christmas rose from 9.7% a week ago to 12%. At the same time, the implied chance of bitcoin falling below $70,000 by Christmas dropped from 15.6% to 11%.

Derive is the world's largest DEX by notional volume and open interest, according to data source DefiLlama.

Still, it is much smaller than centralized giant Deribit, which has been in business for a decade and registers volume and open interest worth several billions of dollars every day. Over there, 25-delta skews for both bitcoin and ether are negative at the front end. In other words, puts are pricier than calls, indicating a bias for downside protection. Stay alert!

Today’s signal

The chart shows ether’s daily price swings in candlestick format since June. Overlaid is the Ichimoku cloud, an indicator used to identify support, resistance and trend changes.

Ether is on the verge of crossing below the cloud and losing support of the bullish trendline from late June lows.

A dual breakdown, if confirmed, would signal major demand-side weakness and mark the end of ether’s bullish structure, paving the way for deeper losses.

title: Bitcoin holds near $80,000 as oil retreats and the Fed decision looms
summary: Bitcoin was little changed near $80,400 since midnight UTC while the DeFi index was the only CoinDesk index to gain, with the Fed due to decide on Wednesday.
content:
3 分で読む

要約

  • Bitcoin steadied near $80,400, little changed since midnight UTC, after dipping to around $79,300 during the Asian morning.
  • The DeFi index was the only CoinDesk index to gain, with uniswap and ethena rising despite Arthur Hayes’ weekend sale of his fund’s directional book.
  • The Fed, which raised rates in September, decides on Wednesday, with CME’s FedWatch tool showing a 90% chance of no change.

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 steadied near $80,400 after dipping to around $79,300 during the Asian morning, leaving it little changed since midnight UTC. Altcoins were mixed, with ether ETH$2,490.55 dropping 0.2% and the DeFi index (DFX) the only CoinDesk index to gain. The tone was set at the weekend, when Arthur Hayes said his Maelstrom fund sold its entire directional book, including 6,400 ether due to macro and geopolitical risk.

S&P 500 index futures rose around 0.3% after Friday’s selloff in U.S. stocks, while oil retreated, with U.S. crude falling around 2% to near $101 a barrel and Brent slipping to around $110 as Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran on Sunday and President Donald Trump said there would be no strike that day, though he kept the option open.

The Fed, which raised interest rates in September, decides again on Wednesday. The CME’s FedWatch tool shows a 90% chance of no change and around an 80% chance of another increase in December. Spot bitcoin ETF flows are also in focus after $138 million of outflows on Friday, taking the two-day exit to $772 million, according to data from Farside Investors.

Derivatives positioning

  • Crypto futures take a breather: Open interest (OI) rose 0.85% to $139.9 billion in 24 hours while volume fell 1.78%. Liquidations dropped 71% to $153 million. The long/short taker volume ratio split of 50.34% to 49.66% shows no tilt.
  • Bitcoin barely moved and positioning barely changed: The BTC price rose 0.20% and open interest rose 0.84%, so only a small amount of money came in. Volume fell 7.21%. Ether looked the same, with open interest up 0.45% and the price adding 0.23%.
  • Funding is mildly positive across the board, with no crowded corner: The 24-hour heatmap for major cryptocurrencies is a uniform green. USDE and TRX sit at the low end. Nobody is paying a heavy premium to hold longs, meaning demand for leverage is nothing out of ordinary.
  • ZEC added money as the price rose: Open interest grew 8.17% and the price advanced 3.84%, so about 4% of new money came in. Volume rose 19.11%. Funding of 0.0063% is modest, so the new positions are not expensive to hold.
  • ENA's rally drew money: Open interest rose 16.85% over 24 hours against an 8.36% price gain, with volume up 81.51%. The past hour showed a 2.04% fall in open interest. Some of the money that came in during the rally has started to leave.
  • Crude is the only top-20 market with negative funding: The funding rate in crude perps is -0.0077%. The price fell 1.55% and open interest dropped 7.37%, so money left as the price declined. Volume jumped 190.88%. The positions that remain lean short.
  • Market-order flow paints a mixed picture: The OI-normalized cumulative volume delta (CVD) for XMR, ZEC, GRAM, CC and SOL is positive, a sign that market-order buying is outweighing market-order selling in these markets. Tokens such as DOGE, LINK, HYPE, XLM have negative CVDs.
  • BTC put skew intact: The busiest contract was the Oct. 28 $77,000 put, ahead of the Oct. 28 $84,000 call. The one-month skew fell to about 12.5% from about 14.5%, so puts still cost more than calls, albeit by less than a day ago.
  • ETH puts dominate volume: Four of the top six contracts were puts, led by the Oct. 29 $2,000 strike. The one-week skew dropped to about 8.7% from about 13.3%, so here, too, puts still cost more than calls.

Token talk

  • Uniswap (UNI) rose 1.9% and ethena (ENA) around 1%, shrugging off Saturday’s sale of 323,000 UNI and 14 million ENA by Arthur Hayes’ Maelstrom fund.
  • AI-linked tokens lagged more broadly, with grass GRASS$0.6352, a data network for AI training, dropping 2.7% and near NEAR$5.2772 losing 1.4%. The moves coincided with Elon Musk’s Sunday warning that lenders have shut off credit to the 200 or so AI-only cloud providers.
  • Hyperliquid (HYPE) rose around 1%, with traders still digesting Friday’s decision by Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), the Nasdaq-listed company that holds the token, to more than triple its share buyback to $100 million, a program that applies to PURR stock only.
  • CoinMarketCap’s Altcoin Season index stands at 53/100, down from 58 on Friday.

title: CoinDCX Confirms $15.99M USDT Loss After Failed Sweep Hit Old Crypto Wallets
summary:
Key Takeaways: CoinDCX announced a $15.99M USDT loss from the old wallet infrastructure in the last contaminated security event impacting the platform in 2025. The exchange said that an automated
The post CoinDCX Confirms $15.99M USDT Loss After Failed Sweep Hit Old Crypto Wallets appeared first on ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • CoinDCX announced a $15.99M USDT loss from the old wallet infrastructure in the last contaminated security event impacting the platform in 2025.
  • The exchange said that an automated sweeping program malfunctioned, and that deposits were made at an old address and then lost.
  • Customer balances, withdrawals and active trading systems did not get affected, said CoinDCX of the loss suffered by it.

Indian crypto exchange CoinDCX has confirmed losing nearly $16 million in USDT after funds accumulated in wallet infrastructure the company had already retired following an earlier security breach.

This revelation immediately follows on-chain research of suspicious transfers from addresses associated with CoinDCX, which questioned the logic of receiving deposits while wallets allegedly deemed “deprecated”.

  • CoinDCX Says Failed Wallet Sweep Caused $15.99M Loss
  • Old Deposit Addresses Were Still Receiving Crypto
    • On-Chain Data Challenged the ‘Deprecated Wallet’ Label

CoinDCX Says Failed Wallet Sweep Caused $15.99M Loss

According to CoinDCX, they noticed unusual transactions on October 21 and also spied on unusual fund transfers through blockchain information and community reports.

During the investigation, it was revealed that the activity had an impact on old operating wallet infrastructure that had been affected in the July 2025 incident. A backend service which used to sweep incoming deposits on those addresses into secure CoinDCX wallets went offline for a period, causing coins to pool there.

The loss of USDT was CoinDCX’s loss of 15.99 million USDT, which the exchange reported that it covered. The exchange has stated that their existing wallets and trading systems are not impacted. The company reported trading and deposits and withdrawals were seamless, and assets held by users were still demand-deposited in segregated cold-wallet custody.

Read More: Initia Halts L1 and Rollups After $2.7M Exploit Tied to Unauthorized Token Minting

Old Deposit Addresses Were Still Receiving Crypto

Despite providing notice to update the deposit address, some users are continuing to send coins to older deposit addresses, CoinDCX said.

Its recovery system was divided into two parts: when the funds were sent to an old wallet, users were credited, and a subsequent automated service transferred them to the main secure wallets of CoinDCX.

The expensive incident highlighted the problems with retaining access to previous compromised wallet infrastructure. If the sweeping process fails, deposits may stay in addresses whose security exposure is known.

On-Chain Data Challenged the ‘Deprecated Wallet’ Label

Blockchain researchers have raised questions about the workings of the less active wallets. According to Bitquery, one address held approximately $15.82 million of USDT and the company tracked 15.99 million USDT in 40 CoinDCX-related Tron wallets. It was a routine deposit-related operation through its investigation up to the day of the incident.

Additionally, approximately $9.63 million was traced to addresses that were linked to Binance, OKX and Gate across a period of about 18 hours. CoinDCX has not responded in public about the source of the unauthorized party unlocking these funds.

The authentication was made just days after CoinDCX CEO Sumit Gupta challenged the initial breach reports.

The flagged addresses were from infrastructure breached in 2025 and Gupta had said that the new ones were a “false alarm” in terms of concerns. Later, CoinDCX has publicly admitted that it has been still interacting with those addresses, which were handling its own deposits.

title: Binance Founder CZ Makes Shocking Claim About AI Hacking: “No Crypto Wallet Is 100% Safe”
summary: Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao has warned crypto users against assuming any wallet is completely secure, arguing that artificial intelligence could intensify security threats without breaking blockchain cryptography.
content:
Skip to content

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao has warned crypto users against assuming any wallet is completely secure, arguing that artificial intelligence could intensify security threats without breaking blockchain cryptography.

The comments followed two X posts in which CZ discussed the limits of digital security and AI risks, highlighting phishing and social engineering as potential threats to crypto holders.

CZ Warns of AI-Driven Crypto Security Risks

On October 23, Zhao challenged concerns that artificial intelligence could directly compromise Bitcoin’s cryptographic protections. He argued that fears about AI hacking cryptocurrency networks overlook the risks facing traditional internet and financial systems.

AI can threaten crypto holders through sophisticated phishing and social engineering attacks that exploit leaked personal data without compromising core cryptography. Source: @cz_binance via X

“Everyone worried about AI hacking crypto, but the internet and banking systems rely on weaker encryption,” CZ wrote.

He also explained how attackers could exploit AI without having to defeat the cryptography protecting digital assets. “AI doesn’t need to break Bitcoin’s cryptography to cause damage; leaked data already enables more phishing, social engineering, etc.,” he added, ending the post with “Stay SAFU.”

The distinction is important. AI-assisted attacks can use personal information exposed through data breaches to create convincing messages, impersonate trusted contacts, or imitate legitimate customer-support teams. A victim who follows a fraudulent link or reveals a wallet recovery phrase can lose funds even when the underlying blockchain and its cryptographic systems remain uncompromised.

Zhao’s comparison between crypto encryption and the protections used by banks and internet services should not be treated as a universal technical assessment. Security depends on the specific algorithms, implementations, account safeguards, and methods used to protect sensitive information.

Recent Hardware Wallet Incidents Highlight Self-Custody Risks

Zhao’s warning comes amid two separate hardware-wallet security incidents reported in 2026. The cases illustrate how cryptocurrency can be stolen through weaknesses in a device’s supply chain or software, rather than through a direct attack on a blockchain’s cryptographic foundations.

CryptoBilis faces scrutiny after researchers linked a hardware wallet incident to over $90 million in crypto losses. Source: Bloomberg via X

In October, Ledger investigated cryptocurrency thefts linked to devices sold through CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller. Blockchain analytics firms estimated that the incident involved approximately $93 million to $95 million in stolen assets, although the figures were not confirmed as a final loss total by Ledger.

Ledger confirmed finding an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one affected device. Reports indicated that the tampered hardware could capture users’ recovery phrases during setup and transmit the information to attackers. Tether subsequently froze $10 million in USDT linked to the thefts, according to published reports.

A separate incident involving Coldcard Bitcoin hardware wallets demonstrated a different type of vulnerability. A flaw in seed generation affected certain devices and reduced the randomness protecting wallet keys, potentially making affected wallets vulnerable to brute-force attacks.

TRM Labs reported in August that the exploit had drained approximately 1,816 BTC, worth about $116 million at the time, from more than 5,200 addresses. The vulnerability originated in older firmware, meaning that installing an update alone would not repair recovery phrases generated under the affected conditions.

Neither incident establishes that AI cracked Bitcoin’s cryptography. Instead, they show how implementation errors, compromised hardware, and weaknesses in wallet setup can expose assets even when users choose tools designed for offline storage.

Why No Crypto Wallet Is Completely Safe

On October 22, Zhao published a broader security reminder stating, “No crypto wallet is 100% safe. No software is bug-free. No tech is 100% secure.”

He also noted that risk exists in both action and inaction, urging users to stay informed, manage risk, and address problems as they arise. The message reflects an important distinction in cryptocurrency security: controlling private keys directly removes reliance on an exchange for custody, but it also places greater responsibility on the wallet owner.

CZ issued a crypto security warning amid reported 2026 hardware wallet incidents involving a Ledger supply-chain attack and a Coldcard firmware flaw, highlighting risks beyond core cryptography. Source: @cz_binance via X

A self-custody wallet does not store cryptocurrency in the same way a physical wallet holds cash. Instead, it manages the private keys or recovery information required to authorize transactions recorded on the blockchain. Anyone who obtains the necessary credentials may be able to transfer the assets, and blockchain transactions generally cannot be reversed simply because a user was deceived.

Hardware wallets can reduce exposure to internet-connected devices, but they are not immune to manufacturing defects, compromised distribution channels, or flawed software. Similarly, software wallets can be affected by malicious applications, device malware, and stolen credentials. The appropriate level of protection depends on how the wallet is created, stored, accessed, and maintained.

Using a centralized exchange introduces a different set of trade-offs. Customers rely on the platform’s custody controls and operational security, while self-custody gives users direct control but requires them to protect their own keys and backups. Neither approach eliminates every form of risk.

How Crypto Holders Can Reduce AI Hacking Risks

Zhao’s warning points to practical precautions rather than a guarantee of perfect security. Users should treat unexpected messages, urgent account warnings and unsolicited requests to verify a wallet with caution, even when the communication appears professionally written or refers to personal details.

Recovery phrases and private keys should never be shared with another person, entered into an unfamiliar website, or sent through email and messaging services. Users should also verify official website addresses, avoid installing wallet applications from untrusted sources, and consider phishing-resistant authentication methods, including compatible hardware security keys, for accounts that support them.

Hardware-wallet buyers should use the manufacturer’s official store or a trusted, authorized distributor and inspect devices for signs of tampering. If a device or recovery phrase may have been compromised, simply updating its software may not be sufficient. Moving assets to a wallet created with a new, secure recovery phrase may be necessary, provided the transfer is carried out safely.

Regularly reviewing security guidance and keeping devices updated can help reduce exposure to known vulnerabilities. However, users should understand what an update fixes and whether existing keys or recovery phrases remain at risk.

CZ’s central message is that cryptocurrency security requires ongoing attention, not blind confidence in a particular device or technology. As AI tools become more capable, the immediate concern for many holders may be increasingly convincing fraud and the exploitation of personal information, rather than an attacker directly breaking blockchain encryption.
